article_title: Xcos on Web as a promising learning tool for Bachelor's of Electromechanics modeling of technical objects
citation: Y. O. Modlo, S. O. Semerikov. (2015). Xcos on Web as a promising learning tool for Bachelor's of Electromechanics modeling of technical objects. http://xcos.fossee.in/
title: Xcos on Web — a cloud service for building imitative models of technical objects in a mobile Web browser
description: Xcos on Web is a web service that lets users build imitative simulation models of technical objects, including electromechanical systems, directly in a mobile Web browser. Its main window contains a model-building area and a block palette — a library of elements that are dragged into the model area and connected by link lines. The article presents it as the tool that solves Scilab Cloud's lack of Xcos access, with the project goal "відтворити повнофункціональну версію Scilab Xcos з доступом через мобільний Web-браузер". The article demonstrates it with a DC motor model built in the service.
requirements: Access through any mobile Web browser; the project aims to reproduce full Scilab Xcos functionality
constraints: The project is still at the preliminary development stage, so not all block settings are available
target_learning_goals: Modeling of technical objects, including electromechanical systems
examples: The article shows a DC motor model built in Xcos on web, with blocks dragged from the palette and connected by lines, and an XML fragment of the model representation
key_sources: Y. O. Modlo, S. O. Semerikov. (2015). Xcos on Web as a promising learning tool for Bachelor's of Electromechanics modeling of technical objects. http://xcos.fossee.in/

article_title: Computing Scattering Cross Sections For Spherically Symmetric Potentials
citation: Anil Khachi. (2024). Computing Scattering Cross Sections For Spherically Symmetric Potentials. https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.18643
title: An Xcos (Scilab) block-diagram environment for solving the Riccati-type phase function equation
description: The article describes a Scilab-Xcos implementation of the Variable Phase Approach for computing phase shifts. Xcos is 'a Scilab toolbox dedicated to the modeling and simulation of hybrid dynamic systems' with a GUI block-diagram editor, offering 'a step-by-step procedure for learning to solve complex differential equations interactively'. The author states that 'For the first time, an Xcos environment has been created to solve the Riccati type non-linear differential equation', with Xcos models given in supplementary material.
requirements: Requires Scilab, open-source numerical software freely downloadable for Windows, Linux and Mac OS
Requires specification of the potential U(r) and energies through k for each partial-wave channel
constraints: Presented for spherically symmetric phenomenological potentials in nuclear, atomic, and molecular scattering
target_learners: physics students and instructors learning scattering theory
target_learning_goals: understanding how potentials affect scattering phase shifts
solving differential equations numerically and interactively
examples: Xcos schemes shown for the Kronig-Penney periodic potential, attractive/repulsive Yukawa potentials, and their combination, with phase-shift plots generated from 'remarkably simple' code
key_sources: Anil Khachi. (2024). Computing Scattering Cross Sections For Spherically Symmetric Potentials. https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.18643
